title: Karnataka Takes Tourism Roadshows to Manchester, London and Birmingham
excerpt: Led by Tourism Minister Kelachandra Joseph George, the UK programme pairs WTM London with diaspora-city roadshows as the state works to revive declining NRI footfall, The Hindu reported.
body:
• Karnataka Tourism runs a UK roadshow programme this week: Manchester on Monday, November 2, World Travel Market London from November 3 to 5, and Birmingham on Friday, November 6, 2026.
  • The delegation is led by Tourism Minister Kelachandra Joseph George, with KSTDC chairman Srinivas M and Tourism Secretary Dr. V. Ram Prasath Manohar, according to the official announcement.
  • NRI visits to Karnataka's tourist places have fallen by more than half since before the COVID pandemic, a senior tourism official told The Hindu — reviving that footfall is the point of the UK outreach.
  • For UK-based NRIs planning a Karnataka trip, the trade push is aimed at getting Karnataka built into more UK-sold India itineraries — the practical effect to watch is new packaged routes beyond Bengaluru.

Karnataka is taking its tourism pitch to Britain this week. The state will run roadshows in Manchester and Birmingham alongside a presence at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, in a focused programme to strengthen engagement with the UK travel trade, build industry partnerships and promote Karnataka among international travel professionals, according to the official Karnataka Tourism announcement.

The Hindu reported the roadshows in a sharper frame: the state is trying to revive declining NRI tourist footfall. The UK is home to one of the largest Kannadiga communities outside India, and diaspora travellers — who combine family visits with leisure touring — are a segment Karnataka does not want to keep losing to better-marketed states.

Why the state is worried

The decline is steep. A senior Tourism Department official told The Hindu that before the COVID pandemic many NRI tourists visited Karnataka, but the number visiting the state's tourist places has since fallen by more than half — and those travellers are now going instead to the Maldives, Bali, Abu Dhabi and other destinations in the Middle East. This is the first time the roadshows are being held in Manchester and Birmingham, the official said. Beyond NRIs, the department is also targeting foreign tourists from London, Germany, the US and Australia, and officials hope the roadshow will lift NRI arrivals by the end of this year or the start of the next tourism season. Around nine people have been selected for the promotion effort, which uses posters and audio-visual displays of Karnataka's tourist places, The Hindu reported. WTM London itself is a large stage: around 180 countries participate, with more than 4,000 exhibitors and over 40,000 participants.

The week's schedule

The programme opens with the Karnataka Tourism Roadshow in Manchester on Monday, November 2, at The Edwardian Manchester, a Radisson Collection Hotel, at Free Trade Hall, Peter Street. It brings together travel agents, tour operators and destination management companies from Manchester and the surrounding region, with destination presentations followed by dedicated B2B sessions.

From November 3 to 5, the delegation moves to WTM London at ExCeL London, where the Karnataka pavilion is at Stall No. N10-528. The week closes with a second roadshow in Birmingham on Friday, November 6, at the Radisson Blu Hotel, Birmingham — a city with a large South Asian population and a natural audience for the diaspora pitch.

Who is going

The delegation is led by Kelachandra Joseph George, Karnataka's Minister for Tourism. He is accompanied by Srinivas M, Chairman of the Karnataka State Tourism Development Corporation (KSTDC); Dr. V. Ram Prasath Manohar, IAS, Secretary to Government, Tourism Department; Shivaprasad P.R., IAS, Managing Director of KSTDC and Commissioner of Karnataka Tourism; and Janardhana H.P., Joint Director, Department of Tourism, along with tourism stakeholders from the state.

What success would look like

The stated aims are concrete and trade-facing: persuade UK operators to include Karnataka in the India itineraries they sell, gather market feedback, and open new collaborations. For diaspora travellers, the test is whether that produces bookable Karnataka product in the UK market — heritage circuits beyond the standard golden-triangle routing, and packages that pair a Bengaluru family visit with Hampi, Coorg or the coast. If you are planning travel, the state's official tourism channels are the place to check what new UK-market itineraries emerge from this week's B2B meetings.
